title: Crewbrain — demo
ttsInstructions: Speak like a calm, confident product founder walking a colleague through a live demo. Plain and warm, measured pace, no hype. Leave a short natural pause between sentences.

segments.name: opening
segments.narration: Meet Sam. Every job depends on what's in his head, and what's on his phone. Here's the same question, asked of two helpers. The homeowner's helper says it can't share crew details. The crew's helper answers, in Spanish. Crewbrain turns company knowledge into voice helpers, with the right access, only for as long as it's needed.

segments.name: brain
segments.kicker: 1 · One company brain · Powered by HydraDB
segments.headline: Snap it. Approve it. Lock it.
segments.caption: Every item keeps its source and its lock.
segments.narration: It starts with Sam's company brain, powered by HydraDB. Everything happens in one conversation, by voice or text. He snaps the warranty card from a SunPeak panel. Claude drafts a knowledge item, and Sam approves it with a tap, locked to homeowners. It sits in the brain with its source, next to the crew brief, and the office-only price book.

segments.name: create
segments.headline: Say the job. Approve the card.
segments.caption: The creator asks only what's missing.
segments.narration: Next, Sam asks for a helper for the Patels, about their install at forty-two Oak Street. The creator asks only for what's missing, like when their access should end. Thirty days after handover. Then the approval card: who it's for, what it knows, what it can do, and when it ends. One tap, and Juno is live. Links go out by text, email, or QR. Rex, for Bay Roofing's crew, takes ten seconds more.

segments.name: work
segments.headline: Answers with sources. Real actions.
segments.caption: Juno cites the warranty. Rex answers in Spanish and logs damage.
segments.narration: Anita Patel opens Juno, and asks what her warranty covers. Juno answers from the approved card, with the source right there. On the roof, Marco picks Spanish and asks Rex by voice. Rex answers in Spanish. Then Marco snaps a photo of a cracked flashing. Rex logs the issue, and it lands in Sam's inbox, with the photo, the note, who sent it, and when.

segments.name: escalate
segments.headline: Questions go to Sam. Answers come back.
segments.caption: Sam answers once. It becomes knowledge.
segments.narration: When Juno can't answer, the question goes to Sam. He asks what's new, and replies in one line. The answer goes straight back to Anita, and it's saved as new knowledge, so the brain keeps getting better.

segments.name: proof
segments.narration: Now the proof. Here is the same HydraDB query, run as two audiences. The crew sees the site brief. The household never does. And the price book doesn't come back for either.

segments.name: locks
segments.headline: Close the job. Access ends.
segments.caption: Another company sees nothing. Closing a job ends every link.
segments.narration: In the app, Juno declines the crew code. Another company on the same server sees nothing of Rivera's. And when the roof is done, Sam says: close Rex. He confirms. Marco asks Rex again, and the helper has ended. The site brief goes back to office only.

segments.name: how
segments.narration: Under the hood, every request passes server policy checks first. HydraDB is the permissioned knowledge: one database per company, an access list on every source, and search that runs as the audience. Claude does the reasoning and takes the actions. And OpenAI's gpt-realtime gives everyone a live voice.

segments.name: close
segments.narration: Sam's phone is quieter now. We're inviting small contractors to the pilot. Crewbrain: your company's know-how, on every job, with the right access, for the right amount of time.
